item.title: Why the US Shouldn’t Pledge Long-Term Military Support for Israel
item.description: President Donald Trump should not forego the military aid leverage needed to bring Israel in line with US foreign policy. The post Why the US Shouldn’t Pledge Long-Term Military Support for Israel appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: America’s Caribbean Crackdown Is Testing the Laws of War
item.description: President Trump’s seizure of The Centuries, a Hong Kong-owned cargo ship, appears to be a flagrant violation of international law. Why did he do it? The post America’s Caribbean Crackdown Is Testing the Laws of War appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Pakistan Is Rushing to Build a Modern Navy
item.description: Pakistan’s development of the new Babur-class corvette is being matched by a similar Indian naval buildup, raising fears of an arms race. The post Why Pakistan Is Rushing to Build a Modern Navy appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Egypt’s New Artillery from South Korea Is a Warning to Israel
item.description: Egypt’s recent military buildup has been focused on Israel, whose war in Gaza poses a dire threat to Cairo’s national security interests. The post Egypt’s New Artillery from South Korea Is a Warning to Israel appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: From Quebec 1775 to Trump 2025: America’s Long Obsession with Owning Canada
item.description: The United States has long sought to possess its northern neighbor—but each attempt has ended in failure. Today, President Donald Trump is trying again. The post From Quebec 1775 to Trump 2025: America’s Long Obsession with Owning Canada appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: After Months of Deployment, the USS Annapolis Returns Home
item.description: The USS Annapolis fast-attack submarine operates out of Guam in the Indo-Pacific—and would be on America’s first line of defense if a major conflict erupted there. The post After Months of Deployment, the USS Annapolis Returns Home appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Who’s Afraid of the Tomahawk Missile? Nigerian Terrorists, Apparently
item.description: The Tomahawk has been a mainstay of the US missile arsenal for more than four decades—and has remained relevant to the modern era, as the weekend’s strikes in Nigeria show. The post Who’s Afraid of the Tomahawk Missile? Nigerian Terrorists, Apparently appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Did Japan Send Fighter Jets to Europe?
item.description: Though Europe has a long military history in Asia, it is quite rare for an Asian nation to send ships or aircraft to Europe, as Japan did earlier this year. The post Why Did Japan Send Fighter Jets to Europe? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Donald Trump’s Pakistan Reset Is Not the End of “India First”
item.description: Relations with Pakistan still lack the necessary depth for a strategic re-orientation of US South Asia policy. The post Donald Trump’s Pakistan Reset Is Not the End of “India First” appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: New Year’s Eve 1942 Was the Day of Hitler’s Biggest Arctic Fiasco
item.description: The Battle of the Barents Sea should have been a triumph for Nazi Germany. Instead, it ended in the destruction of its surface fleet—and Admiral Erich Raeder’s career.
